title: GIAC GCIH
summary: GIAC GCIH (Global Information Assurance Certification Certified Incident Handler) is an advanced, vendor-neutral certification centred on detecting, containing, eradicating and recovering from security incidents, including the adversary techniques that create them. It targets experienced security operations analysts, incident responders, forensic examiners and consultants who already understand host and network fundamentals and now need to run an investigation from first alert to final report under time pressure. Passing the exam demonstrates to an employer that the holder can triage an alert stream, form and test a hypothesis, preserve perishable evidence before shutdown, contain a live intrusion without destroying the evidence that explains it, and communicate findings that a non-technical stakeholder can act on. The exam is proctored and open-book, using multiple-choice and multiple-answer items with a scaled passing score, and scenario-style questions dominate: candidates are asked to choose the next correct action or interpret a short artefact rather than recite a definition. Hands-on practice is decisive. Responders who have personally walked through live-response triage, timeline reconstruction, memory and disk acquisition, and containment decisions on systems they built and broke will recognise the intended answer quickly, whereas candidates who rely on courseware alone frequently misread which phase a question sits in and select an action that is sound in general but wrong at that moment. GCIH is generally treated as evidence of operational readiness rather than theoretical knowledge of response process.
objectives: Incident response lifecycle: Apply preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery and post-incident review to a live intrusion, and justify each decision against the phase it belongs to.
Adversary techniques and tradecraft: Interpret common initial access, execution, persistence, privilege escalation and lateral movement behaviour from the defender's position.
Detection and triage: Build hunt hypotheses, prioritise alerts and separate true positives from environmental noise using host, network and identity telemetry.
Volatile evidence handling: Order the collection of memory, process, network and session state so perishable evidence survives before any shutdown or remediation step.
Host and memory investigation: Interpret process trees, autostart locations, services, scheduled execution and memory artefacts to identify malicious execution and persistence.
Network evidence and containment: Use flow and packet evidence to scope an intrusion, then contain it without alerting the adversary or corrupting the record of what happened.
Malware and tooling triage: Characterise suspicious binaries and scripts safely, describe observed behaviour, and decide what to block, isolate or hunt for next.
Eradication and recovery: Verify removal of adversary access, restore services in a controlled order, and define the monitoring that confirms the environment stays clean.
Communication and reporting: Produce timelines, findings, confidence statements and recommendations that serve both technical peers and executive decision makers.

batches.title: GCIH Batch 1: Incident Alert Triage and Hypothesis-Driven Scoping
batches.focus: Detection & Triage: log and alert analysis, SIEM-style queries, prioritisation, blue-team lens.

batches.focus: Response & Hands-on: terminal emulator, configuration and policy completion, decision trees, spot-the-mistake, incident timeline ordering.

batches.focus: Adversarial & Cross-domain: red-team perspective, evasion, dual-perspective pairs, ATT&CK mapping, risk ranking, report drafting.
